name: Post-Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitor Sexual Dysfunction
aliases: Persistent Sexual Dysfunction after SSRI Discontinuation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Post-SSRI Sexual Dysfunction

criteria.description: Presence of sexual dysfunction symptoms persisting for at least 3 months after discontinuation of SSRI treatment
Documented history of SSRI use for at least 4 weeks prior to symptom onset
Exclusion of other medical, psychiatric, or pharmacological causes of sexual dysfunction
Symptoms began during SSRI treatment and persisted after discontinuation
Symptoms include decreased libido, erectile dysfunction, anorgasmia, or genital anesthesia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria must be met: persistent sexual dysfunction for at least 3 months post-SSRI discontinuation, documented SSRI use, and exclusion of other causes.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical; no definitive laboratory or imaging tests exist.

pathognomonic.notes: Numbness or reduced genital sensation persisting after SSRI cessation
Inability to achieve orgasm despite adequate stimulation
searchTerms: inability to reach orgasm despite treatment

pathognomonic.notes: Impaired ability to attain or maintain erection after stopping SSRI

common.notes: Reduced sexual desire lasting beyond SSRI treatment
Prolonged time to ejaculation persisting after SSRI discontinuation
Insufficient vaginal moisture during sexual activity
Reduced tactile sensation in genital area

occasional.notes: Psychological distress secondary to sexual dysfunction
Mood disturbances potentially exacerbated by sexual dysfunction
Reduced tactile sensation localized to the penis
Dyspareunia possibly related to lubrication deficits

rare.notes: Swelling of genital tissues without clear etiology
searchTerms: genital edema that does not go away

rare.notes: Rare cardiovascular symptom reported during sexual activity
Transient weakness reported by some patients
searchTerms: reduced muscle strength with sexual activity

other: Clinical diagnosis based on history and exclusion of other causes

distinguishingFeatures: Symptoms present prior to SSRI use
May have identifiable organic or psychological causes
Sexual dysfunction coincides with active depressive episodes
Different temporal relationship to symptom onset

redFlags: Sudden onset of genital pain or swelling
Signs of major depressive episode or suicidal ideation
New cardiovascular symptoms during sexual activity
references: Bostwick JR. Post-SSRI sexual dysfunction: a literature review. Psychopharmacology (Berl). 2019;236(5):1353-1367.
Healy D, Le Noury J. Sexual dysfunction and SSRIs: a review of the evidence. Int J Risk Saf Med. 2018;29(1-2):1-14.
Orphanet: Post-Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitor Sexual Dysfunction. ORPHA:686475.
